quotes.text: Balance is not eating perfectly. It is eating well often enough that the occasional treat is just that.
No single food makes you unhealthy and no single food makes you healthy. The pattern does.
You can enjoy the mithai at the wedding and still eat well this week. Both are true.
A strict plan is a sprint, and sprints end. A balanced one is a way of living, and it continues.
Food is not a moral test. A plate is just a plate.
Eating well has room for the birthday cake, and for the vegetables the day after.
All-or-nothing is the quickest way to end up with nothing.
Balance has room for a samosa, a salad, a second helping of dal and a quiet Tuesday.
Half of the plate can be colourful. The rest can be whatever you love.
Give the foods you love a place in your week and they lose their power over you.
When every food is forbidden, every food becomes an event. Let things be ordinary.
One heavy meal does not undo a good week, just as one good meal does not undo a heavy one.
Deprivation is a loan against future cravings, with heavy interest.
Enjoying dessert without guilt is a skill, and it is part of eating well.
Aim to feel good after you eat, not just while you eat. Then let yourself have both when you can.
A day of eating out does not need a day of punishment. It needs the next normal meal.
Making up for a big meal by skipping the next one is a trap. The next meal just needs to be a normal one.
Moderation is not boring. It is the reason you can keep enjoying things.
Let one meal be a party and the next a quiet one. Life moves in both tempos.
Do not skip a meal to make room for a treat. Eat normally and enjoy the treat as well.
Some days are full of vegetables and some days are full of jalebi. Life is long enough for both.
The healthiest relationship with food is a relaxed one.
Balance is not never leaning. It is leaning back to the middle, again and again.
Aim for most days, most meals, most of the time. Not all of them.
Choose the food that satisfies, not just the one that fills. Sometimes that is the salad. Sometimes it is the ladoo.
Eating well is a spectrum, not a switch.
Where you are today is not a verdict. It is a starting line, and everyone has one.
Make peace with the plate in front of you, then make the next one a little better.
Taste, nourishment and joy all belong at the table.
If a plan makes you dread food, the plan is wrong, not you.
You do not need to earn dessert, and you do not need to burn it off. Enjoy it, then carry on.
A steady middle path beats a heroic sprint followed by a collapse.
Two chapatis, a bowl of dal, a plate of sabzi and a spoon of curd is a perfectly good dinner. Simple, and complete.
Protein, plants and something you enjoy. Most meals need little more than that.
Variety is the closest thing to a nutritional secret. Try one new vegetable this week.
Colour on the plate is an easy way to cover your bases without counting anything.
When you eat with friends, let the company be the main dish.
Perfection is not the goal. Feeling good on most days is.
A plate does not have to be perfect to be a step forward.
Restriction works for a week. Balance works for years.
There is no need to eat like a saint on weekdays to be forgiven for weekends. Just eat like a person.
A treat you enjoy slowly is worth three you finish in a hurry.
Enough is a wonderful amount. Learn to recognise it and to stop there, happily.
It is not the festival that matters for your health. It is what you do on the ordinary days around it.
Healthy is not a look and not a number. It is a way of eating that you can enjoy for a long time.
Food can be pleasure, nourishment and company all at once. Do not ask it to be only one.
You are allowed to eat something just because it is delicious, and you are allowed to eat something just because it is good for you.
Big plates of good food, small portions of rich food, and no lectures. That is a fine place to start.
Nothing tastes as good as a treat enjoyed without a running commentary.
The middle path is not the boring path. It is the one you can walk for the rest of your life.
